title: Patterned invagination prevents mechanical instability during gastrulation.
authors: Vellutini, Bruno C; Cuenca, Marina B; Krishna, Abhijeet; Szalapak, Alicja; Modes, Carl D; Tomancak, Pavel
one_liner_zh: 该文研究果蝇胚胎原肠胚形成中机械力与形态发生演化，虽涉及转录因子buttonhead表达，但核心是组织形态发生而非蛋白质-DNA互作建模，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Mechanical forces are crucial for driving and shaping tissue morphogenesis during embryonic development(1-3). However, their relevance for the evolution of development remains poorly understood(4). Here we show that an evolutionary novelty of fly embryos-the patterned embryonic invagination known as the cephalic furrow(5-7)-has a mechanical role during Drosophila gastrulation. By integrating in vivo experiments and in silico simulations, we demonstrate that the head-trunk boundary of the embryo is under increased compressive stress due to the concurrent formation of mitotic domains and germ band extension and that the cephalic furrow counteracts these stresses, preventing mechanical instabilities during gastrulation. Then, by comparing the genetic patterning of species with and without the cephalic furrow, we find evidence that changes in the expression of the transcription factor buttonhead are associated with the evolution of the cephalic furrow. These results suggest that the cephalic furrow may have evolved through the genetic stabilization of morphogenesis in response to the mechanical challenges of dipteran gastrulation. Together, our findings uncover empirical evidence for how mechanical forces can influence the evolution of morphogenetic innovations in early development.
abstract_zh: 机械力对于胚胎发育过程中组织形态发生的驱动和塑造至关重要(1-3)。然而，它们与发育演化的相关性仍知之甚少(4)。在此，我们展示了果蝇胚胎的一个演化新颖性——称为头沟 (cephalic furrow) 的图案化胚胎内陷(5-7)——在果蝇原肠胚形成中具有机械作用。通过整合体内实验和计算机模拟 (in silico simulations)，我们证明胚胎的头-躯干边界因有丝分裂域和胚带延伸的同时形成而处于增加的压缩应力下，且头沟抵消了这些应力，防止原肠胚形成期间的机械不稳定性。然后，通过比较有头沟和无头沟物种的遗传图案化，我们找到证据表明转录因子buttonhead表达的变化与头沟的演化相关。这些结果提示，头沟可能通过形态发生的遗传稳定化演化而来，以应对双翅目原肠胚形成的机械挑战。综合来看，我们的发现为机械力如何影响早期发育中形态发生创新的演化提供了实证证据。
